title: How handicap weights are determined — Eliminations
note: BHA explains that every race has a maximum permissible field size/safety factor and that excess declared horses are eliminated or balloted out under race-specific elimination rules.

title: 152nd Longines Kentucky Oaks — 2026 stakes conditions
note: Current 2026 race conditions cap the field, designate up to four also-eligible horses, state how the highest-preference also-eligible replaces a scratched starter, and explicitly state entry fees and preference criteria.

title: Racing Explained — Glossary
covers: Backstretch / Back Straight; Rails; Right-Handed Track
note: The current glossary directly defines Backstretch/Back Straight as the far-side straight and also provides current racecourse terminology for rails and right-handed/clockwise tracks.

title: What is the Parade Ring?
note: The Jockey Club directly describes the Parade Ring/paddock as the pre-race area where runners meet jockeys and parade before racegoers, while distinguishing the pre-parade ring.

title: A guide to horse racing
note: The current raceday guide describes winning and placed horses entering the Winners’ Enclosure after a race and the owner presentation that follows.

title: ウイナーズ・サークル
note: JRA directly defines ウイナーズ・サークル as the winning-horse presentation area, supporting the generic post-race presentation-enclosure concept without asserting one worldwide facility name.

title: コーナー
note: JRA's current facility glossary explicitly identifies the ホームストレッチ as the stand-side straight and the バックストレッチ as the opposite/far straight while explaining course geometry.

title: Australian Harness Racing Rules — Starting
note: The Australian harness rules use mobile barrier for the moving starting apparatus and define participation in a mobile start by facing the mobile barrier when it begins to move.

title: Starting Regulations — Mobile Starts
note: HRNZ mobile-start regulations specify construction and operation of the Mobile Barrier vehicle and extended arms; use as New Zealand harness terminology evidence rather than a universal apparatus rule.
